notes.claim: The exponential distribution is the only distribution with a constant failure rate.
After early failures, the failure rate levels off and stays roughly constant for the majority of a product's useful life.
The inverse of the failure rate, 1/lambda, gives the mean time to failure, more commonly called the MTBF in the power industry.
With an MTBF of 1 million hours, only 36.7 percent of units are statistically likely to operate that long.
A diesel generator in its useful life period is assumed to have a constant failure rate while running.
